dialogue.commons.scene.supper.endorsed/1: The shearing supper is three weeks off. I have been counting chairs since spring.
dialogue.commons.scene.supper.endorsed/2: You will be here for the supper, I hope. Long table, everyone cooking, nobody eating alone.
dialogue.commons.scene.supper.endorsed/3: We have the shearing supper coming. It is the one night the whole place is in one room.
dialogue.commons.scene.supper.endorsed.r: I'll let you get back to it.
dialogue.commons.scene.supper.endorsed.e: Two tables end to end, and whoever sheared most is served first. That is the whole ceremony.
Everybody brings a dish and nobody says whose is whose. It works better that way.
It runs late, there is singing, and somebody always falls out over the seating. Then it is done for a year.
dialogue.commons.scene.supper.endorsed.w: Good. Come hungry and come early, we start before dark.
I will put a chair out, then. You will know half the table by the end of it.
That pleases me more than it should. Bring nothing, we always have too much.
dialogue.commons.scene.supper.questioned: The shearing supper is coming round again. I will go. I always go.
Everyone is talking about the supper. It is a great many people in one room, is all I will say.
I have nothing against the supper. I find the week after it easier than the night itself.
It does sound like a lot.
Too many people, and too much owed afterwards. Somebody always keeps a tally.
I like the village. I like it best in twos and threes, not all at once.
It is the noise, mostly. And having to be pleased for four hours together.
Thank you. Most people tell me I will enjoy it once I am there.
It is a relief to hear somebody say so out loud.
Then we can both stand near the door and be no trouble to anybody.
dialogue.commons.scene.borrowed_tool.act: I lent %3$s to %2$s a fortnight back. I do not mind, exactly, but I would like it seen to.
%2$s still has %3$s. That is how it goes here, and it is also how things go missing.
Somebody will ask me for %3$s this week and I will have to say %2$s has it.
You have known %2$s longer than I have. That settles it for me.
If you say %2$s is good for it, I will stop counting the days.
Right. I will ask plainly next time I see %2$s, and think no worse of them.
%2$s. It was a fair ask at the time, and %3$s was sitting doing nothing.
It went to %2$s, in the wet week. %3$s would only have rusted here.
%2$s came round for %3$s and I said yes without thinking about it much.
dialogue.commons.scene.borrowed_tool.set: %3$s came back. %2$s brought it round in person, sharpened.
That is done. %2$s returned %3$s and stayed for a cup.
%3$s is back on its hook. %2$s was as good as their word.
It is. I will stop making a small saga out of %2$s now.
Squared away. %2$s is where it belongs and nobody fell out over it.
Done with. I will lend %2$s again, which is rather the point of the thing.
dialogue.commons.scene.mill.hearsay/1: %2$s told me about %3$s at the mill. I have not seen it myself, mind.
dialogue.commons.scene.mill.hearsay/2: There is talk of %3$s down at the mill. I had it from %2$s, for what that is worth.
dialogue.commons.scene.mill.hearsay/3: %2$s says there was %3$s. I would not repeat it as fact.
dialogue.commons.scene.mill.hearsay.sour: From %2$s, and %2$s was not there either. So take it as talk.
%2$s heard it from somebody at the mill. That is two people between me and it.
Only %2$s. I asked the same question you did and got no further.
dialogue.commons.scene.mill.hearsay.kept: Yes. Best left where it is until somebody who was there says otherwise.
Agreed. I should not have carried it this far, if I am honest.
That suits me. It is not mine to be spreading about.
dialogue.commons.scene.village.evergreen: It is a quiet place. It keeps what it keeps and argues about the rest.
Nothing much. The village goes on being the village.
Same as ever, which after the years I have had here I will take.
Small, stubborn, and better than it looks from the road.
People here will lend you anything and then talk about it for a month.
We manage. Everyone knows everyone else's business, and mostly that is a kindness.
dialogue.commons.followup.thanked/1: Thank you for asking. Not everybody does.
dialogue.commons.followup.thanked/2: Appreciated. I will let you get on.
dialogue.commons.followup.thanked/3: That is good of you. Come by again.
dialogue.commons.leaving/2: Mind the bell post, it leans.
dialogue.commons.plain.respond: It is a small place and it keeps its own habits. You get used to them.
